summary.short: Utah HB 464 amends the state's electronic communication harassment offense (Sec. 1) and enacts a civil action by minor account holders or their parents against social media companies for adverse mental health outcomes linked to excessive use of algorithmically curated services (Secs. 2-7), effective May 1 and October 1, 2024.
summary.long: Amends Utah Code 76-9-201 (electronic communication harassment). Defines terms and makes it an offense, with intent to intimidate, abuse, threaten, harass, frighten or disrupt, to repeatedly contact a person, insult or threaten them, overload an electronic communication system, or publish or misuse personal identifying information; violations are class B or class A misdemeanors. An adult who publicly discloses a minor's personal identifying information while consciously disregarding a substantial risk of resulting harm commits a class A misdemeanor, and a minor victim has a civil right of action for damages, attorney fees and costs. Enacts 78B-3-1101 to 78B-3-1106 creating a civil action by a Utah minor account holder or parent against a social media company for an adverse mental health outcome diagnosed by a licensed provider and caused by excessive use of an algorithmically curated social media service. Claimants receive a rebuttable presumption of causation. A company that limits minors' use to three hours per 24 hours, blocks access from 10:30 p.m. to 6:30 a.m., requires parental consent and disables engagement driven design elements is entitled to a rebuttable presumption of no causation. Recovery is the greater of $10,000 per outcome or actual damages, plus fees and costs. Waivers of these protections are void. Section 8 repeals Sections 13-63-101 to 13-63-701. Part 11 takes effect October 1, 2024; other provisions take effect May 1, 2024.

obligations.summary: A person may not, with intent to intimidate, abuse, threaten, harass, frighten or disrupt, engage in the listed electronic communication conduct (repeated contact, insults or threats, system overload, or posting or misusing another person's personal identifying information). Penalties are coded under enforcement, not here.

evidence.quote: a person is guilty of electronic communication harassment and subject to prosecution

obligations.summary: To obtain the rebuttable presumption against liability, a social media company must demonstrate that it limits a Utah minor account holder's use to no more than three hours in a 24-hour period, restricts access between 10:30 p.m. and 6:30 a.m., requires parental or guardian consent to use, and disables engagement driven design elements. The company must also remain liable to ensure the account is subject to these restrictions, even when device-level settings are used.
obligations.conditional_on: to obtain the rebuttable presumption in Sec. 78B-3-1103(4), the company must demonstrate compliance with Sec. 78B-3-1104(1)

evidence.quote: disables engagement driven design elements for a Utah minor account holder's account

Coded on social media companies as the parties whose contract terms are invalidated.
